articles.title: Ukraine says Russia bombed apartment block as birthday gift for Putin
articles.summary:
Building in Pryluky destroyed, killing nine people including three children, officials say, night before Russian president’s 74th birthday

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia’s military…

blocks.text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia’s military of deliberately killing civilians and bombing residential buildings as a macabre gift for Vladimir Putin, who celebrates his 74th birthday on Wednesday.
Ukraine’s president described Russia’s overnight drone and missiles strikes, which killed at least 24 people, as “despicable”. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively,” he said.

Video showed a ballistic missile slamming into a five-storey apartment block in the town of Pryluky in the northern Chernihiv region. The concrete building collapsed, entombing those inside. Eighteen people died, including four children, officials said.

Zelenskyy identified them as Oleksandr, Kyrylo, and Serhii, who was one year old, as well as eight-year-old Maksym. He said five children were among about 50 people who were injured. Rescuers continued to pick through the rubble, with several residents not yet accounted for, he added.

“Today, on Putin’s birthday, the Russian army ‘presented’ him with the destruction of a residential block in Pryluky,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media. “The Russians know very well that they are striking ordinary cities, ordinary life. It is an absolutely deliberate choice of terror.”

He acknowledged Ukraine was struggling to shoot down enemy ballistic missiles, and appealed to allies to provide US-manufactured Patriot interceptors. “Air defence packages for us right now are a vital necessity,” he said.

blocks.caption: People carry a casualty after the attack on Pryluky. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters

blocks.text: The bombardment featured 70 ballistic missiles, as well as 46 jet-powered drones, which in recent weeks have been terrorising Ukrainians on a daily basis. Ukraine’s air force said it managed to down more than 80% of the fast-moving drones – an improvement on the previous average of 50% to 60%.

Eleven regions were hit. Two people were killed in Kyiv, with other deadly strikes in the central cities of Kremenchuk and Oleksandriia, where four civilians died. There was also extensive damage in Dnipro.

Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, said Russian generals had given Putin his favourite birthday present: “war crimes”. Moscow’s grim strategy of bombarding the country’s population so it capitulated would not work, he said.

“The Ukrainian people are not going to give up, because it’s about Ukraine’s survival as a nation and as a state,” he said. The “ultimate” present would be a dock in The Hague, home to the international criminal court, where the Russian president would stand trial, Sybiha said.

One resident in Kremenchuk said the attack happened early on Wednesday. The woman told Ukrainian media: “We were making tea in the morning. My husband was getting ready for work. And that was it. I found myself on the floor. What can I say? It was very scary.”

Local people in Dnipro said a blast wave affected 16 buildings, blowing out doors and windows. One woman, Iryna, said her auto parts workshop had been hit for the sixth time. The ceiling collapsed in Wednesday’s strike, she said, with toilets, sinks and equipment damaged.

“The explosion happened around three in the morning. We were sleeping at home. Everyone was scared, probably the whole city heard it. We will restore the shop and continue to work,” she told the Suspline channel.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine had carried out its own long-range strikes on economic and military sites inside Russia. They included two oil complexes and a training ground in the ⁠Perm, ​Samara ‌and Astrakhan ‌regions.“These are ‌justified Ukrainian responses to ​all Russian attacks on ⁠our people,” ​he said.

The president posted dramatic video of a burning oil tanker close to the southern resort city of Sochi. Russian officials said naval drones had hit the Liberian-flagged ship, adding that “crude oil was burning openly on the Black Sea”. Its Indian crew of 23 was rescued, they said.

Both sides have heavily targeted commercial shipping around the Black Sea since Putin’s full-scale invasion in 2022. In recent weeks Russia has picked off vessels carrying Ukrainian grain, paralysing maritime traffic from Ukraine’s southern ports including Odesa.

Earlier this week, a civilian cargo ship sank after a suspected attack by Russian drones in the Black Sea. Its crew is still missing. A second vessel carrying grain was also hit while sailing in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, said the Bulgarian prime minister, Rumen Radev. The search for survivors was called off on Wednesday, according to Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov of the Maritime Administration Executive ⁠Agency. “There are no ​traces of the sailors from the ‌first ship, and there will ‌be none,” he said.

articles.title: LA officials document first case of a rabid raccoon in more than 50 years
articles.summary:
Four people and a dog may have been exposed to rabies from the animal, Los Angeles public health officials say

Los Angeles county recently documented its first rabid raccoon in more than 50…

blocks.text: Los Angeles county recently documented its first rabid raccoon in more than 50 years, and health officials are urging residents to never touch wild animals.

The county’s department of public health announced in a statement this week that four people and a dog may have been exposed to the animal at a back yard work site in the city of Westlake Village. The raccoon appeared in ill-health but was not aggressive.

Rabies is spread through a bite or scratch from an infected animal. It kills tens of thousands of people each year, mostly in Africa and Asia, and is almost completely fatal once symptoms appear. The US sees less than 10 deaths annually “due to robust prevention efforts”, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Health officials in Los Angeles county told residents they should “always keep a safe distance from wildlife and contact your local animal control if you encounter an animal that appears sick, injured, or is behaving unusually” and ensure pets are up to date on their vaccines.

“The detection of rabies in a raccoon is an important reminder to never touch, handle, or feed any wild animals, even when they appear healthy,” said Dr Muntu Davis, the Los Angeles county health officer.

The group of people who were possibly exposed to rabies in Los Angeles county were receiving follow-up care, which includes a series of vaccines. The dog was up to date on its rabies vaccine and is “doing well” under quarantine, according to the health department.

It is not yet known which rabies variant the raccoon was infected with, although officials believe it was likely rabies from a bat. The county has not had a documented case of a rabid raccoon since 1973, according to the public health department, and the last known animal, aside from bats, to have rabies was a skunk in 2014.

This year, the county has seen the highest number of rabid bats it has ever recorded, the public health department said last week, with 69 documented cases. The sick animals have been found in every part of the county and nearly a third of all bats submitted for rabies testing were infected.
“Rabid bat detections can vary year-to-year, but Los Angeles county has seen a steady upward trend for more than a decade,” the public health department said.

articles.title: Former UBC professor tells defamation trial he was 'shocked' by sexual assault accusation
articles.summary: Author and former UBC professor Steven Galloway says he was "shocked" to learn he was being accused of sexual assault, and believed he had split amicably after an affair with the former student…

image.caption: Author and former UBC professor Steven Galloway is seen through a window as he leaves B.C. Supreme Court during a break at his defamation lawsuit, in Vancouver, on Oct. 6. (Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Author and former UBC professor Steven Galloway says he was "shocked" to learn he was being accused of sexual assault, and believed he had split amicably after an affair with the former student making the allegation.
Steven Galloway told Vancouver court he believed he had split 'amicably' with former student after affair

Galloway told a B.C. Supreme Court judge in his lawsuit alleging defamation that the relationship was "inappropriate, ill-advised and stupid," but they'd maintained a friendship and regular contact after they split in 2013.

His legal action alleges the woman, whose identity is protected by a publication ban, and others repeated the allegations online and defamed him, setting off the loss of his job at the university as a professor and chair of the creative writing department.

Galloway testified he'd had a two-year consensual relationship with A.B., a former student who was older than him, whom he'd met sometime in 2011 when she took a writing course from a colleague of his.
Former UBC professor Steven Galloway’s defamation trial begins

He told the court that he'd learned of the sexual assault allegation while he was in Ohio for an event in November 2015, and spoke with Annabel Lyon, who was acting chair of the creative writing department in his absence.

He says Lyon kept asking if he was suicidal, then police showed up to his hotel room on a report that he was a danger to himself and others, and he was handcuffed and committed to a psychiatric hospital for 72 hours.
"I kept saying to her, 'no, I'm fine.' At one point, I said, 'Annabel, don't worry. I'm way too much of a coward to kill myself,' and that's the kind of sense of humour I have."
"The next thing I know, there's a knock on my door, and it's the police."

items: Steven Galloway defamation trial begins in B.C. Supreme Court
Defendant apologizes to B.C. writer days before defamation trial to start

blocks.text: Galloway said he didn't know where he was or what was happening, and "then I got put in the most terrifying place I've ever been in my life."
Earlier in the hearing on Tuesday, Galloway's wife testified that her husband was "gutted" after being accused of rape, and became extremely distraught as he repeatedly denied the allegations.
Katie Wagner told the court that before Galloway was accused of sexual assault, suspended, then fired from his teaching position, he was extroverted and socially active in the literary community.
She said he stopped playing piano and reading and writing after his career was derailed by the allegations, that would resurface repeatedly online after he was suspended in November 2015.

"He lost his writing career when he was accused of sexual assault, when every single time we tried to put out a different sort of thing, somebody came back and said that it was a sexual assault," she said.
"His whole world was about the Canadian literary community."
Galloway is pictured in his former office at UBC in Vancouver on March 31, 2014. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
Justice Neena Sharma began the second day of the trial in Vancouver by granting continued anonymity to the defendant in the long-running defamation case, first filed in 2018.

The judge said A.B. has shown that identifying her would carry objective harms and specific risks, and allowing anonymity is in line with protecting the privacy and dignity of sexual assault complainants.

Sharma said the woman has withdrawn her defence of her statements against Galloway as justified, but has not admitted that her accusations are false and the court can’t make assumptions until it hears all evidence.
The court heard on Monday that the woman received hateful and vitriolic messages after she was identified in news articles related to the author’s lawsuit.
A.B. had sought an indefinite order to keep her identity under a publication ban, but Sharma's order will expire within six weeks of a ruling in the case, although she can apply to extend it.

Sharma said A.B. is not participating in the trial due to her fragile mental state, which has included suicide attempts, though she's shown "resilience" dealing with past proceedings before the trial.
The court has heard from both Galloway's and A.B.'s lawyers about their clients' mental health struggles, including suicide attempts, in the years since the accusations became public.
Galloway’s lawsuit was originally filed against numerous defendants who allegedly defamed him online and in other forums by repeating unproven allegations of rape.
The court has heard that four defendants remain.

Kids Help Phone: 1-800-668-6868. Text 686868. Live chat counselling on the website.

articles.title: German politicians warn of antisemitism on October 7 anniversary
articles.summary: Leading German politicians including Chancellor Merz and President Steinmeier called for people to reject antisemitism.

image.caption: Demonstrations were held across Germany commemorating victims of the October 7 attacksImage: Fabrizio Bensch/REUTERS

blocks.text: High-ranking German politicians marked the anniversary of the terrorist attacks that took place in Israel on October 7, 2023.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke about doing more to fight antisemitism within Germany, while also pressing for a two-state solution between Israelis and Palestinians.
"We are witnessing rising antisemitism in Germany — antisemitism that far too often goes unchallenged," Merz said, adding that his government "will do everything" to combat it.

"Jewish people must be able to live without fear throughout Germany," Merz said in a statement, also emphasizing Germany's support for Israel. "Our Israeli friends can count on our commitment to ensuring that such a crime never happens again."
'Political action' needed
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said antisemitism in Germany "flared up in an intolerable manner since October 7."

"Germany must continue to stand up against antisemitism and for Israel’s security, for the dignity and self-determination of the Palestinians, and for the prospect of peaceful coexistence in the Middle East," he said in a statement.
Federal Parliamentary Speaker Julia Klöckner commemorated the day by emphasizing that more needs to be done to combat antisemitism through "political action."
"Antisemitism should not be allowed to have a place on our streets or our political debates," she said.

blocks.caption: Germany Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Israel in December 2025Image: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany stands with Israel

Some 1,200 people were killed in the attack, carried out by Palestinian militant group Hamas and its affiliates, while 251 people were kidnapped to Gaza, in the deadliest attack on Jews since the end of the Holocaust.
More than 74,000 people have been killed in the Gaza Strip in Israel's war following the attack, with some countries and human rights groups saying Israel is committing genocide against Palestinians.
Demonstrations were held across Germany for victims of both the Hamas attacks and the Israeli war that followed.

In Berlin, a crowd of around 1,700 people, many waving Israeli flags, gathered at Bebelplatz, according to police estimates. Israeli Ambassador Ron Prosor and German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt also attended. Bebelplatz was the site of Nazi book burnings following the party's seizure of power in 1933.

Germany has supported Israel throughout the war, although Merz did halt of delivery of some military equipment to Israel following growing legal concerns over the war in Gaza, including arrest warrants issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant.
Although Germany is a party to the treaty that created the ICC, Merz vowed not to arrest Netanyahu should he travel to Germany.
How did the October 7 attacks change Israel?

articles.title: Israelis demand accountability over 7 October failures three years after attacks
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take any personal responsibility for what happened or order a state inquiry.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Residents of Kfar Aza attended a memorial ceremony on Wednesday for those killed on 7 October 2023
ByLucy Williamson
Middle East correspondentReporting fromJerusalem and Kfar Aza
As the sky began to lighten over Israel's border with Gaza on Wednesday, the people of Kfar Aza moved silently towards the armoury at the centre of the kibbutz.

It was there, shortly after 07:00 on 7 October 2023, that Hamas-led attackers killed half the community's 14-member civil defence squad. They were among 64 killed and 19 kidnapped from the community that day.
The pain of those attacks is still fresh here. But three years on, there are questions about who else should pay the price for Israel's security failure.
"I need my country to take responsibility," said Inbar Goldstein, whose brother and niece were killed, and four other relatives kidnapped from Kfar Aza.

The 7 October attack was the deadliest Israel had suffered since its creation in 1948. About 1,200 people were killed across southern Israel by gunmen who broke through the border fence and attacked communities there. Another 251 people were taken back to Gaza as hostages.
Three years on from Israel's biggest security failure, there is still no independent state inquiry into how it was allowed to happen.

And the man in charge at the time of that failure - Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu - is running for election again, with the same campaign promise: to be stronger and tougher than anyone else in protecting Israel from its enemies.
"Nobody investigated the roots [of the attack]. It didn't start or end on October 7th - it's a long process of abandonment," Goldstein said.

blocks.caption: Image caption, More than 60 residents of Kfar Aza were killed by Hamas-led gunmen and 19 were taken hostage three years ago

blocks.text: More than 60 residents of Kfar Aza were killed by Hamas-led gunmen and 19 were taken hostage three years ago

Aside from Hamas's responsibility for the attack itself, there are growing questions in Israel around what caused the country's intelligence failure, what information was passed to military and political leaders in the run-up to the attacks, and what Netanyahu himself knew.
For months beforehand, young female soldiers posted at bases along the Gaza border to watch for suspicious activity had warned their superiors about possible preparations for an attack.
Among them was Roni Eshel. She was killed with 14 other members of her unit when gunmen overran their base at Nahal Oz, just next to Kfar Aza.

"There are so many questions," her uncle Elad Levy told me. "Were the Egyptians warning the prime minister? The Emiratis? Were there no other warnings Netanyahu ignored? We need to find out what happened – not just on the day, but the year before, and five years before that."
"The truth should be clear," he continued. "If we don't inquire into this, it will happen again and again."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected any personal responsibility for security failures three years ago

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected any personal responsibility for security failures three years ago
Over the past three years, there have been mounting reports of warnings being given to Netanyahu - by his own security chief, as well as by regional neighbours – which he denies.

Last month, Israel's Haaretz newspaper published extracts from a new book, alleging that the leader of the United Arab Emirates had called Netanyahu 10 days before the attack to warn of Hamas plans for a major operation.
Netanyahu's office has dismissed the report as "an absolute lie" and has said he will sue the newspaper.

Amir Ohana, a member of Netanyahu's Likud party, said in a social media video last month that it was "preposterous and absurd" to suggest that Netanyahu could have known about the attack when the former Hamas leader in Gaza, Yahya Sinwar, had only told a handful of people.
Israel's prime minister, he said, had since reshaped the Middle East and did not give up, "even when voices inside and outside Israel called on him to stop".

Netanyahu has blamed his own security chiefs for the failures that led to the 7 October attacks, accusing them of deliberately choosing not to wake him in the hours beforehand, for fear that he would order a massive deployment of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and escalate the situation.
"God forbid we wake up the prime minister and he says, 'Wake up the entire IDF immediately, scramble the air force!'" he told Israel's right-wing Channel 14 television network.
"What would have happened if they had woken me? This would not have happened," he said, suggesting that his response would have better protected Israel from the attacks.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Netanyahu denied reports that he was warned by the UAE's president days before Hamas attacked

blocks.text: Netanyahu denied reports that he was warned by the UAE's president days before Hamas attacked
Yaacov Katz, a journalist and author of several books on Israel's defence, has written about the growing concerns over Hamas activity that emerged in the hours leading up to the assault.

In his book, While Israel Slept, he describes calls between senior military figures and intelligence chiefs in the early hours of the morning, the sudden recall of commanders from leave, and the dispatch of an elite intelligence unit to the border.
He told me their expectation was, at worst, a small, limited incursion by Hamas fighters.
"So why would [Netanyahu] order a massive pre-emptive strike by the IDF, if every security chief is telling him this is not what this is going to be? Waking him would not have made a difference."
But he said Netanyahu faced other questions about his failure to spot what was happening.

"You were the prime minister, you set the policy," he said. "You created a doctrine and a policy of containment that trickled down to the last soldier manning the watchtower on the border with Gaza: contain Hamas, separate the Palestinians, and keep Hamas in power to prevent the establishment of a Palestinian state."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Israelis have held protests to demand the establishment of a state commission of inquiry

blocks.text: Israelis have held protests to demand the establishment of a state commission of inquiry
For years, Netanyahu oversaw a policy of containing - not confronting - Hamas in Gaza, during which Israeli governments allowed Qatar to provide hundreds of millions of dollars of aid for Gaza.
A month after the 7 October attacks, he told a German newspaper that claims he wanted to strengthen Hamas were "an absolute lie".
"On the contrary we wanted to continue to weaken Hamas as much as we could," he told Die Welt. "But the money was meant to avoid a civilian catastrophe - that is the only reason."
Months after the attack, the IDF's then-chief of staff, Lt Gen Herzi Halevi, publicly apologised for the failure to defend civilians, saying he carried that weight on his shoulders and in his heart.
He resigned. A raft of military commanders were later fired, and Israel's domestic intelligence chief left his position.
Netanyahu has so far rejected any personal responsibility for the attacks.

Col Richard Hecht was the IDF's international spokesman on 7 October. He told me the refusal of political leaders - including Netanyahu - to accept responsibility was part of the reason he resigned six months later.

"It's a disgrace," he told me. "When you look at accountability, within the IDF I don't think there's a problem. And that's the pain. That's one of the main causes of bad blood between the political echelon and the military."
At a memorial ceremony in Jerusalem on Monday, the father of one of those killed on 7 October stood up to challenge the prime minister.
"You didn't protect my son, you didn't protect all those who were murdered," he said, before security guards led him away. "Shame! Disgrace!"

blocks.caption: Image caption, "Netanyahu does not surrender" is a slogan of his right-wing Likud party

blocks.text: "Netanyahu does not surrender" is a slogan of his right-wing Likud party
Three years on from the attacks, calls for accountability are growing. Campaigners have asked Israel's highest court to force the government into establishing a state commission of inquiry.
Yizhar Shai, a former minister and opposition politician whose youngest son Yaron, a soldier, was killed on 7 October, is part of that campaign.

"We are going into these elections almost blindfolded as it relates to October 7th," he told me during a protest in Tel Aviv last week. "Our prime minister has never given a detailed, thorough explanation under oath, where he would be asked all the tough questions and have to explain everything."
Netanyahu has consistently refused a state inquiry led by Israel's Supreme Court, arguing recently that the country's judiciary would be biased against him.
Before calling an election, his government proposed an alternative "national commission of inquiry", whose members would be appointed by political parties.
But despite passing a raft of other legislation before parliament ended its session in July, Israel's government said it ran out of time to pass a bill setting out its plans for the inquiry.
We approached several members of his Likud party for an interview, without success. We also requested that the party respond to their critics, and are waiting for their response.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Gadi Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have backed calls for a state commission of inquiry

blocks.text: Gadi Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have backed calls for a state commission of inquiry
Netanyahu's denial of responsibility has now become an election issue, as he prepares to run for re-election later this month.

A video game called Sleepy Bibi, released by the team of his main opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, asks players to help the prime minister avoid responsibility by dodging warnings of an attack and "making it to bed safely".
Netanyahu has styled himself for decades as Israel's "Mr Security", and despite presiding over the worst security failure in Israel's history, is running on the same security platform again.
For the past three years, he focused on waging new wars against Israel's enemies - Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran.
Polls suggest a close race, and that the 7 October attacks are central to many voters' decisions.
Yaacov Katz says the legacy of 7 October is a coin with two sides.

"There are the failures, the mistakes that led to the Hamas invasion," he told me. "But there's the other side, which is Netanyahu's argument; that [he] has re-engineered the Middle East and made Israel a safer place today. And that is an argument Israelis take with them to the polls."
The shadow of the attacks hangs over this election, dividing Israel once again along political lines.
For supporters, it confirms that Benjamin Netanyahu is still needed to keep Israel safe.
Critics say his political survival puts Israel at risk.

articles.title: Stronger primary, preventive care for Pinoys sought
articles.summary: Sen. Bong Go has urged the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. to further strengthen primary and preventive health care while ensuring adequate benefits for Filipinos undergoing dialysis and other…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
PhilHealth acting president and CEO Dr. Beverly Ho said roughly P100 billion out of about P400 billion in total disbursements accounts for dialysis.
Businessworld / File

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Bong Go has urged the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. to further strengthen primary and preventive health care while ensuring adequate benefits for Filipinos undergoing dialysis and other life-sustaining treatments following PhilHealth’s disclosure that around 25 percent of its payouts goes to dialysis.
She stressed that earlier management of hypertension and diabetes could help prevent kidney disease from progressing to the point that patients require regular dialysis.
Go said the figures underscore the need to invest more aggressively in keeping Filipinos healthy before illnesses become severe and more difficult to treat.
“Let us take care of our health while it’s early and not wait for the condition to worsen, including hypertension and diabetes,” Go said.
He stressed that efforts to prevent chronic kidney disease should not come at the expense of patients who already depend on dialysis.
“To those needing dialysis, support must be sustained. We are talking about lives here. We should not hold back on spending for health care,” he said.
Go said PhilHealth funds should be maximized for the direct benefit of its members, particularly ordinary Filipinos who often struggle with health care expenses.
“PhilHealth funds are the people’s money, from their contributions. We must return it to them through quality health care,” Go said.
“Every peso, every centavo. It’s their money,” he added.

Go had strongly opposed the transfer of PhilHealth funds to the National Treasury and welcomed the return of P60 billion following a Supreme Court ruling, reiterating that money intended for health care must remain for the health needs of Filipinos. The high court unanimously ordered the return of the transferred amount and permanently prohibited the transfer of the remaining P29.9 billion.

Ho described PhilHealth’s investment in primary care as a strategic approach to the long-term sustainability of the national health insurance fund, pointing out that dialysis can also affect patients’ ability to work because treatment requires regular sessions.

articles.title: DepEd to include mathematics in ARAL program expansion
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) will expand its Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning Program to include Mathematics in an effort to sustain gains in the Program for International Student…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
This file photo shows a facade of the Department of Education.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) will expand its Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program to include Mathematics in an effort to sustain gains in the Program for International Student Assessment 2025.“The latest PISA results showed us that real progress is possible when we focus on foundational skills, but it also served as a clear reminder of how much ground we still need to cover,” Education Secretary Sonny Angara said.
Under DepEd Memorandum 060, Series of 2026, the ARAL Mathematics program aims to improve core numeracy skills among learners from Grades 1 to 10.

“With ARAL Mathematics, our goal is simple: to reach every learner, wherever they are in their learning journey. Whether a child needs help recognizing basic numbers or mastering algebraic concepts, we are building a system that gives them targeted, flexible support so no learner gets left behind,” Angara said.
The program will address learning gaps through diagnostic profiling using the Rapid Mathematics Assessment.
Tutors will track learners’ progress through an Individual Mathematics Intervention Plan to provide tailored support.

“Reading opens the door to knowledge, while mathematics builds the logic and critical thinking our youth need for the future. By combining structured practice with flexible scheduling, we are ensuring our schools have the tools to turn early learning wins into lasting academic resilience,” Angara said.
Under the guidelines, tutoring groups must maintain a ratio of 10 to 15 learners per tutor to maximize individual attention.
Instruction will prioritize self-paced learning, allowing learners to work independently through structured worksheets while tutors serve as facilitators rather than traditional lecturers.
Nationwide implementation in all public schools will begin in the second term of the school year 2026-2027.

articles.title: 80% of Pinoy children face violence – CEAP
articles.summary: Eighty percent of Filipino children have experienced some form of violence at home, school, workplace, community or in dating relationships, the Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
A child raises her hands to cover her face.
Pexels / Ksenia Chernaya

MANILA, Philippines — Eighty percent of Filipino children have experienced some form of violence at home, school, workplace, community or in dating relationships, the Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines (CEAP) revealed as it called for stronger child protection measures in Catholic schools through a protocol.

“The CANE+D Protocol, covering Child Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination, should be a serious concern for Catholic education because the scale of violence against children in the Philippines tells us that child protection cannot remain at the level of policy statements,” CEAP said.

The association noted that aside from the 4th National Plan of Action for Children report, the United Nations Children’s Fund reported that three in five children experienced violent discipline, about one in three experienced school bullying and one in five children who use the internet have experienced sexual abuse or exploitation online.

In 2023 alone, the Philippine National Police Women and Children Protection Center received 18,756 reports of child rights violations, of which 17,304 involved violence against children, including child abuse, rape and acts of lasciviousness.

“These figures remind us that a school may be one of the places where a child first discloses harm or where warning signs are first seen. The revised CANE+D protocol therefore matters because it establishes a more coordinated pathway for identification, reporting, investigation, case management, legal proceedings, rehabilitation, reintegration and prevention,” CEAP added.
CEAP said the protocol brings teachers and other frontline workers into the protection system and calls for specialized training for personnel handling CANE+D cases.

The Department of the Interior and Local Government has directed local government units to adopt and implement the revised CANE+D Protocol and strengthen coordinated referral and case-management systems involving social workers, law enforcement, health professionals, educators and other frontline actors, CEAP said.

“For Catholic schools, this is ultimately a question of mission: when the dignity of a child is wounded, how prepared are we to recognize it, respond to it, protect the child and walk with the child toward healing?” it asked.

“Healing, therefore, cannot mean simply helping a child feel better after something has happened. In Catholic education, healing must include protection, truth, accountability, accompaniment, restoration, and the rebuilding of trust,” CEAP said.

articles.title: Palace seeks probe on Gracioso’s claims
articles.summary: Malacañang has called for a deeper probe into the claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that he delivered more than P2 billion in cash to Vice President Sara Duterte and members…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Calire Castro
The Philippine STAR / Noel Pabalate

SINGAPORE – Malacañang has called for a deeper probe into the claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that he delivered more than P2 billion in cash to Vice President Sara Duterte and members of her family on the instructions of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Palace press officer Claire Castro said evidence would show who is credible among those making conflicting claims.
She said Gracioso has shown that he was with the Vice President in some “personal” events.

“The investigation on this should be deeper, not for anyone but for the people because this involves public funds. Even if they claim that this is just politicking and that is their sole defense, those who are investigating this should not be stopped,” Castro said at a press briefing here.?
Duterte has denied Gracioso’s claims, saying the former policeman’s statements may have been motivated by money.
Velasco’s camp refuted the accusation, dismissing it as a “one-size-fits-all” narration “designed and fabricated to attack as many targets as it can while being inconsistent with verifiable events.”
Meanwhile, Duterte’s camp lashed back at Castro over the latter’s statement that the Vice President knows alleged bagmen Ramil Madriaga and Gracioso.
“No one prevents anybody from playing dumb. But it’s embarrassing,” defense spokesman Michael Poa said. - Bella Cariaso

articles.title: COA upholds disallowance of P73.29 million OVP secret funds
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit has affirmed with finality the disallowance against the Office of the Vice President (OVP)’s P73.29 million in confidential funds that were spent in just 11 days in…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
The photo of the Commission on Audit's office in Quezon City.
The STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Audit has affirmed with finality the disallowance against the Office of the Vice President (OVP)’s P73.29 million in confidential funds that were spent in just 11 days in December 2022.

In a 15-page decision dated Oct. 5, the COA denied for lack of merit the motion for reconsideration filed by Vice President Sara Duterte, special disbursing officer Gina Acosta and OVP chief accountant Julieta Villadelrey.
It upheld its April 10 ruling that affirmed the notice of disallowance issued by the COA Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office on Aug. 8, 2024.
“The office has already anticipated the possibility of this decision and has prepared to respond through the appropriate legal and institutional channels,” the OVP said.
The OVP, however, said it has yet to receive a copy of the Oct. 5 COA resolution.
The notice covered expenses made from Dec. 21 to 31, 2022, from the total of P125-million confidential funds that the OVP received on Dec. 20 that year.
The disallowed amount included P69.787 million in rewards and P3.5 million in payments for tables, chairs, desktop computers and printers.
According to the notice, rewards were paid out as P10 million in cash, P34.857 million in various goods and P24.93 million in medicines.

The COA pointed out that the notice of disallowance was issued due to the failure of the OVP to submit documents showing the success of information-gathering and/or surveillance activities to support the payments of rewards to informers, as required by Joint Circular No. 2015-01 or the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds.
Instead, the COA said the OVP submitted a list of activities that the Vice President and officers of OVP satellite offices attended from Dec. 13 to 31, 2022.
Moreover, the list did not indicate or narrate the accomplishments that resulted from the information gathered or in the surveillance activities.
It also did not give weight to the OVP’s argument that the absence of untoward security-related incidents showed that it had complied with the requirement, saying such “does not hold water.”

The audit body also pointed out that the OVP submitted a certification from the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSG) listing routine security activities such as casing, liaising, surveillance, profiling and ocular inspections.

But the VPSG, as salaried personnel of the AFP, are “fundamentally disqualified” from receiving informer rewards under the joint circular, the COA said, and that submitting acknowledgement receipts for payments to salaried personnel, without proof of operational success from eligible non-employee informers, rendered the P69.787 million “completely unsubstantiated and disallowable in audit.” – Bella Cariaso

articles.title: DOH monitoring Russia outbreak
articles.summary: The Department of Health is closely monitoring developments in Russia involving the death of a laboratory technician at a plague research institute, as well as recommendations from the World Health…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
The fraudulent posts are spreading misinformation, the DOH said.
BusinessWorld / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Health is closely monitoring developments in Russia involving the death of a laboratory technician at a plague research institute, as well as recommendations from the World Health Organization (WHO).

The DOH said it is prepared to respond should additional measures become necessary, citing a recent evaluation that affirmed the country’s capacity to meet the requirements of the International Health Regulations.

“The Bureau of Quarantine is ensuring that travelers are appropriately screened and that vector surveillance for rodents and rodent fleas on incoming cargo and vessels is strictly implemented. We will keep everyone apprised should additional measures become warranted,” DOH said on Tuesday.
Malacañang yesterday gave assurance that health authorities are monitoring developments.

The DOH response comes after the WHO said the risk of an epidemic in Russia remained low following the death of Darya Shipilova, 28, who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia. – Alexis Romero

articles.title: House OKs P7.2 trillion 2027 budget bill
articles.summary: The House of Representatives has approved on second reading the government’s proposed P7.2-trillion spending plan for fiscal year 2027.

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
Lawmakers approved through voice vote yesterday House Bill 10858, which contained the proposed national budget for next year.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives has approved on second reading the government’s proposed P7.2-trillion spending plan for fiscal year 2027.
Third reading approval is expected to be on Oct. 12 after House leaders requested the Senate’s permission to extend their legislative calendar to pass the budget bill on final reading.

The floor adopted amendments reallocating around P116 billion from the National Expenditure Program, following recommendations from a select committee of ranking lawmakers to augment flagship state assistance projects and infrastructure.
Of the amount, P8.12 billion went to additional funding for the education cluster and P20.86 billion for the agriculture sector.
Lawmakers also lodged an extra P11.49 billion for infrastructure build up under the Department of Public Works and Highways.
The Department of Transportation received an additional P2.35 billion in realigned funding.

Lawmakers also realigned an additional P25 billion to the Department of Social Welfare and Development’s crisis assistance program. The Department of Health got P24.96 billion for its indigent patient relief program.

articles.title: DA: Rice imports may breach 5 million MT
articles.summary: The country is expected to import more than five million metric tons of rice this year to strengthen supply as domestic production is projected to decline due to the effects of El Niño,…

blocks.text: October 8, 2026 | 12:00am
DA Assistant Secretary Arnel de Mesa said agency projections showed the country will have a 75-day supply of rice by the end of the year to withstand the effects of El Niño.
STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — The country is expected to import more than five million metric tons (MT) of rice this year to strengthen supply as domestic production is projected to decline due to the effects of El Niño, according to the Department of Agriculture.
The Philippines has imported 3.98 million MT of rice as of Sept. 24, which has already surpassed last year’s 3.39 million MT.
Among the top sources of rice was Vietnam at 2.72 million MT, followed by Thailand at 517,528 MT and Myanmar at 400,359 MT.
The DA is projecting a 700,000 MT reduction in total rice production this year because of El Niño.
It added that 163,812 MT or P6.78 billion has already been damaged as of Sept. 26. Most of the affected crops were corn, followed by rice and high-value crops. – Ric Sapnu, Artemio Dumlao

articles.title: Lawyer files injunction seeking to force incoming PQ government to take oath to King
articles.summary: A constitutional lawyer has filed an emergency injunction in an attempt to force the incoming Parti Québécois government to swear allegiance to King Charles.

image.caption: The National Assembly in Quebec City. In 2022, MNAs passed a law putting an end to a requirement to swear an oath to the King in order to sit in the legislature. (Jacques Boissinot/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Montreal·New
A constitutional lawyer has filed an emergency injunction in an attempt to force the incoming Parti Québécois government to swear allegiance to King Charles.
Government should 'not be at liberty to freely flout the laws,' lawyer filing challenge says
The application for an interim stay was filed in Quebec Superior Court by the Public Interest Litigation Institute and its founder, Lawrence David.
David said political parties "regardless of their stripes" are "not at liberty to freely flout the laws that apply to all democratic institutions in Canada.
"That is precisely why we are standing up," David, who teaches at University of Ottawa’s faculty of law, said in an interview.
"We are taking measures using the legal system, which is precisely what the legal system is there for, to ensure that ... governments respect the law that is applicable to them."

The injunction asks the court to immediately suspend a 2022 provincial law that made the oath to the monarch optional for members of the National Assembly. David already filed a lawsuit in August over the same matter.
The latest move comes following Monday's election victory by the sovereignist Parti Québécois.

items: Could the Parti Québécois actually abolish the monarchy in Quebec?

blocks.text: Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has pledged to move to cut funding to the office of Quebec's lieutenant-governor within his first 100 days in power, as part an attempt to "abolish" the monarchy in the province.
The legal filing argues that if the newly elected MNAs refuse to take the oath to the King, they are not constitutionally qualified to sit in the legislature.
The lawsuit warns that any laws passed by an illegally assembled body — especially a law attempting to abolish the lieutenant governor — would be void, creating an "unprecedented legal crisis."

items: Before a referendum, how a new PQ government could test Ottawa

blocks.text: The request will be presented in a Montreal courtroom on Friday morning.
If the stay is granted, MNAs would be legally required to take the oath before taking their seats. The National Assembly is expected to reconvene on Nov. 17.

Karine Millaire, an expert in constitutional law and an associate professor at the Université de Montréal, said in an email the "injunction was to be expected as there is an ongoing constitutional challenge of the 2022 law before courts."
Referring to the emergency injunction, Millaire said the burden will be "on the shoulders of the applicants" to show the case has serious legal arguments.
Ultimately, she said in an email, "these debates on the monarchy could lead to a constitutional crisis, which is not to be hoped [for]."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Benjamin Shingler is a reporter based in Montreal. He previously worked at CTV, The Canadian Press and the New Brunswick Telegraph-Journal. He can be reached at benjamin.shingler@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after botched execution attempt, lawyers say
articles.summary:
Lawyers seek preservation of evidence after prisoner received two doses of pentobarbital on 30 September

Christa Pike, a Tennessee prisoner who survived the state’s attempt to execute her,…

blocks.text: Christa Pike, a Tennessee prisoner who survived the state’s attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said, as they head to court on Wednesday seeking a court order requiring preservation of all evidence relating to the botched exercise by the state.

Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital, a sedative, as Tennessee officials attempted to put her to death last Wednesday in a case that shocked many in America and created headlines around the world. She was set to be the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

“Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking and continues to receive critical medical care. Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery,” attorneys for Pike said in a statement on Tuesday.

Her legal team will ask a court on at a hearing on Wednesday to require the Tennessee department of correction to preserve all “relevant physical, written and electronic evidence” related to the failed execution, court documents said. A press conference is also scheduled.
Her attorneys said they were grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital “who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her”.

“She is the only person known to have survived a complete execution attempt in the US. Christa is a survivor and will take recovery one day at a time. We continue to ask the Governor of Tennessee to commute Christa Pike’s sentence to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole,” Pike’s attorneys added.
The statement was the first indication that Pike has improved since an ambulance carried her away from a Nashville prison on the night of 30 September.

Witnesses to the attempt to execute Pike described how they heard she was choking and struggling for an hour after receiving the first injection. She was then hospitalized after a second dose failed to kill her. In hospital, she was put on a ventilator and had been in critical condition.

Following the botched execution attempt, one of Pike’s lawyers, Randy Spivey, called the process “cruel and torturous”, adding that he had counted seven needles in Pike’s left arm, “one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her”. Her lawyers had warned before the execution that officials might struggle to locate veins and cause her suffering in the process, but the state had pushed to proceed and the US supreme court allowed the prison to move forward.

The disastrous attempt sparked widespread condemnation across the political spectrum and among advocates for banning the death penalty. Tennessee’s prison chief, Frank Strada, also resigned in the aftermath. Strada was facing intensifying scrutiny, with lawyers saying Pike’s case was the fifth “botched” execution under his leadership across two states.
Pike and her boyfriend, who was 17 at the time, killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, one of their classmates at Knoxville Job Corps, in 1995.

According to prosecutors, Pike was worried Slemmer was trying to take her then boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, away from her. Together, they lured Slemmer into a wooded area behind the agriculture campus steam plant at the University of Tennessee on 12 January 1995, tortured and killed her.
Shipp was convicted of first-degree murder in 1997 and was given a life sentence with the possibility of parole.
Pike has never denied her involvement in Slemmer’s killing. She was later diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.
As a child, Pike had been subject to various abuse, including multiple rapes by different men, as well as beatings by her relatives.
Pike later underwent nearly 30 years of solitary confinement while on death row.

In the wake of the botched execution attempt Helen Prejean, a Catholic nun who is perhaps the best-known advocate for abolition of the death penalty in America, told the Guardian: “This is the essence of cruelty. Take a conscious, imaginative human being, give her a date for her death, have her anticipate it over and over again, and then take her out and try and kill her.
“She was rendered defenceless as they deliberately attempted to kill her – what greater mental torture for a human being is there?”
Sam Levin and the Associated Press contributed to this report

articles.title: Teodoro: Ayungin resupply to push through despite China interference
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines will push through with rotation and resupply (RoRe) missions to Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal despite Chinese interference that forced the military to suspend…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines will push through with rotation and resupply (RoRe) missions to Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal despite Chinese interference that forced the military to suspend its latest attempt nearly two weeks ago, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said.

“Definitely, whatever happens, kailangan gawin (we need to do it). That is a principle,” Teodoro told reporters on Tuesday during a visit to the Armed Forces of the Philippines’ Western Command (WestCom) headquarters in Puerto Princesa City.
“And without disclosing details, it has to be done,” he added.
Teodoro declined to discuss plans for the next RoRe mission to the BRP Sierra Madre, saying operational control rests with WestCom.
“’Yan ay kailangang gawin, and nakahanda kami kung saan man, ano man ang plano ng WestCom tungkol diyan,” he said.
(That has to be done, and we are prepared for whatever WestCom’s plan may be.)
The AFP suspended its Sept. 24 RoRe mission to the Sierra Madre after Chinese naval and coast guard vessels challenged Philippine ships much farther from Ayungin than in previous missions.
The military later said three People’s Liberation Army Navy warships, including two Houbei-class missile boats, and five China Coast Guard vessels were monitored during the mission.

Philippine vessels were challenged about 111 kilometers from Ayungin. Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad, AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, earlier said resupply missions had previously managed to reach within about 15 to 19 kilometers of the shoal before encountering Chinese interference.
‘Absolute right’
Teodoro said the Philippines’ position remained unchanged despite the latest confrontation.
“We have an absolute right to do any lawful activity within our exclusive economic zone without the interference or consent of any other foreign power,” he said.
Ayungin is within the Philippines’ 370-kilometer exclusive economic zone and continental shelf.
The Sierra Madre, a World War II-era landing ship deliberately grounded at the shoal in 1999, serves as the country’s military outpost there.
Asked about the troops stationed aboard the aging warship following the suspended mission, Teodoro said their morale remained high.
“Nakaranas na sila ng ganito noong araw, hindi na bago sa kanila,” he said.
(They have experienced this before. This is nothing new to them.)

Teodoro visited WestCom with AFP Chief of Staff Gen. Antonio Nafarrete to receive updates on its operations, including activities in the West Philippine Sea and plans to strengthen the military’s presence in Palawan.
He confirmed that recent confrontations in the West Philippine Sea were discussed during the closed-door meeting but declined to disclose operational details.
Bigger military presence
The defense chief also called for a stronger and sustained military presence in Palawan, including plans for at least a brigade-sized Army presence in the province.

In a statement on Teodoro’s visit, the Department of National Defense said he sought a “significant and meaningful” presence of the military’s three services in the area to support territorial defense, internal security, disaster response and deterrence against unlawful activities.
“Palawan is the last frontier, right? Let’s make sure that it is the last frontier,” Teodoro told WestCom personnel, according to the DND.
The department said efforts were also underway to strengthen the presence and capabilities of the Philippine Army and Marine Corps in Palawan, including a sustainable growth plan for the Marines.

“A Marine Corps is not a Marine Corps if it has no mobility. And that is what we must work hard to allow them to sustain their lethality, their firepower, and their mobility, particularly now in the eastern seaboard where there is no significant presence,” Teodoro said.
In his interview with reporters, Teodoro said officials also discussed Air Force support facilities as the government lays the groundwork for more sustainable operations in the West Philippine Sea.
“At the end of the day, in the future, hindi natin puwedeng panatilihin na ganito lagi ang estado ng ating WPS,” he said.
(At the end of the day, in the future, we cannot keep the situation in the West Philippine Sea this way.)
Teodoro said officials also discussed supporting the “normalization of habitability” on Pag-asa (Thitu) Island, the largest Philippine-occupied feature in the Kalayaan Island Group.
“The issue sa Pag-asa, it’s not totally a security issue na. It is a community-building and sustainability issue,” he said.
Jinan University
Teodoro also rejected criticism that he was attacking Chinese schools following his recent remarks about Jinan University.
“Hindi natin ina-attack ’yung Chinese schools,” Teodoro said. (We are not attacking Chinese schools.)

He said his concerns were specifically about Jinan University, citing its Philippine Studies Center, where he said teachers were trained, and an academic study concerning Batanes that came from the university.
ACT Teachers Rep. Antonio Tinio had criticized Teodoro’s remarks, saying he was amplifying a narrative first raised by maritime security analyst Ray Powell.
Teodoro rejected the suggestion that the government was merely relying on Powell, saying Philippine authorities conduct their own research and information-gathering.
“’Yung ating mga pag-aaral at pagkalap, pagsaliksik, hindi nanggagaling sa isang tao ’yan,” he said.
(Our studies, information-gathering, and research do not come from just one person.)
Teodoro said the government was not accusing anyone but maintained that the matter deserved scrutiny.
“Wala tayong pinaparatangan. Sinasabi lang natin na kailangan masusi nating pag-aralan ’to,” he said.
(We are not accusing anyone. We are only saying that this needs to be studied carefully.) /cb

articles.title: Ex-Barclays traders jailed for rigging interest rates have convictions quashed
articles.summary:
Acquittals of five former bankers come year after supreme court overturned ruling against City trader Tom Hayes

Five more former traders who were jailed for rigging interest rates have had…

blocks.text: Five more former traders who were jailed for rigging interest rates have had their convictions quashed by the court of appeal in London, after a long battle to clear their names.
The court overturned the convictions of Jay Vijay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon and Colin Bermingham – all of whom worked at Barclays.
Their acquittals on Wednesday came just over a year after the UK supreme court overturned a decade-old ruling against the former UBS and Citigroup trader Tom Hayes.
The five former Barclays traders were jailed between 2016 and 2019 on charges of manipulating the euro interbank offered rate (Euribor) or the now-defunct London interbank offered rate (Libor).

The Euribor and Libor rates affected the value of ordinary people’s pensions, mortgages and savings, as well as hundreds of trillions of pounds and euros worth of financial products around the world. Nine bankers accused of rigging the rates were given fraud convictions.

blocks.caption: Jay Merchant leaves Southwark crown court in London during his trial in 2016. Photograph: Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The five former Barclays traders applied to clear their names after Hayes, the first banker jailed for Libor-rigging in 2015, had his name cleared. Carlo Palombo, a former Barclays trader sentenced to four years in prison in 2019 for rigging Euribor, also had his conviction quashed on the same day in July 2025.

The supreme court overturned the convictions of Hayes and Palombo after finding faults in the original trials, ruling that had ultimately “deprived” them of a fair trial. They found trial judges had given “inaccurate and unfair” instructions to the juries that found the former traders guilty.

The cases of the American Pabon; Calcutta-born Merchant; Britons Bermingham and Mathew; and French national Moryoussef were referred back to the court of appeal by the Criminal Cases Review Commission in January.

blocks.caption: Tom Hayes (right) and Carlo Palombo outside the supreme court in London after their convictions were quashed. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

blocks.text: The move came after the Serious Fraud Office (SFO), which brought the original charges against the men, found their convictions “may be considered unsafe” after the supreme court ruling in the cases of Hayes and Palombo. The SFO did not contest the appeals.
Mathew said: “For the last 10 years, the stain of a criminal conviction has been a burden I have carried every minute of every day.”

blocks.caption: Jonathan Mathew, pictured in 2014, said: ‘For the last 10 years, the stain of a criminal conviction has been a burden I have carried every minute of every day.’ Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

blocks.text: He added: “Having this conviction quashed is not simply about correcting the record, it’s about finally having validation that this is an injustice that never should have happened.”
after newsletter promotion
In a statement, Pabon, thanked Hayes, who he said “refused to let it go and pushed this through for all of us”.

Tom Bushnell, a partner at the law firm Hickman & Rose, which represented Merchant, Mathew and Moryoussef, said: “In Jay Merchant and Jon Mathew’s case, it took over a decade for this wrong to be righted. In Philippe Moryoussef’s case, over eight years.

“Their lives have been turned upside down as a result. All involved in the criminal justice system should now ask themselves not only how this error came to be made and repeated, but also why it took so long to correct.”

Wednesday’s ruling marks a further blow for the SFO, with the unravelling of more of its high-profile prosecutions. It said: “After carefully considering this judgment and the full circumstances, ​we do not oppose the appeals ​of five individuals convicted by juries in relation ​to Libor and Euribor.”
The agency reiterated in a statement that the supreme court had “found that there was ample evidence on which a properly directed jury could have convicted Tom Hayes and Carlo Palombo”.
Jason Williams, the head of division at the SFO, added that it was not deemed in the public interest to seek retrials of Hayes and Palombo.

A further attempted appeal by Christian Bittar, a former Deutsche Bank trader who pleaded guilty in 2018, is expected to be heard on Friday. His case is the only one being contested by the SFO, which argues his conviction was safe.

articles.title: Transgressive, edgy DIY: What the 90s meant for British art
articles.summary: The 1990s are remembered for Britpop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the…

image.caption: A new exhibition at Tate Britain takes viewers back to the 90s in BritainImage: Eddie Otchere

blocks.text: The 1990s in Britain are often remembered through a haze of n,ostalgia consisting of rave culture, Britpop and provocative art and fashion by the likes of Tracey Emin and Alexander McQueen.
Undeniably, the decade was a time of major change in British society — the long reign of Margaret Thatcher had come to an end and the West entered a period of relative post-Cold War stability.
Meanwhile, British cultural icons like Oasis, the Spice Girls and Vivienne Westwood garnered international fame.
But Tate Britain's new exhibition "The 90s: Art and Fashion," which opens on October 8 and runs through February 14, 2027, urges viewers to look beyond the familiar names and images.

Even though now prominent artists such as Damien Hirst and Juergen Teller are among the show's 70 contributors, the exhibition also aims to highlight the creative input of those in communities which were left out of the mainstream discourse.

After all, says chief curator Edward Enninful in the exhibition's program, "the energy of the 90s was not concentrated in a single movement, but distributed across communities, disciplines and geographies that have not always been equally represented."

blocks.caption: Fashion editor and style icon Edward Enninful curated the exhibitionImage: Adama Jalloh

blocks.text: An inclusive perspective

For Enninful, the exhibition is personal: The Ghanaian-born British fashion editor, stylist and creative director became the youngest-ever fashion director of i-D Magazine in the 90s at age 18, helping shape the diverse and experimental London fashion scene of the 1990s. He later became editor-in-chief of British Vogue in 2017.

Enninful writes that he and his co-curators aimed to present a body of work which "reflects a broader landscape of practices and voices that shaped the period, many of which operated beyond the structures of visibility at the time." The exhibition pays special attention to artists of color and women whose work was not necessarily showcased as prominently at the time.

Black masculinity became "a site of cultural negotiation" in Britain in the 90s, writes co-curator Helen Little in the program text: "Figures such as Chris Ofili, Steve McQueen, Keith Piper, Koto Bolofo and Ozwald Boateng reimagined the Black masculine, challenging the racist specter of Black men, who had been defined as part of a masculinity crisis linked to post-industrial decline and excluded from the narrative of 'Cool Britannia.'"
Just like "Swinging London" in the 1960s, "Cool Britannia" became a widespread phrase to refer to the 1990s as an era during which British youth culture, pop music, art and political optimism boomed.

blocks.caption: British-Ghanaian/Dominican photographer Eileen Perrier featured women of color who were rarely celebrated at the timeImage: Eileen Perrier/DACS

blocks.text: DIY meets Dr. Martens

The 90s also offered artists plenty of chances to create without waiting for support from traditional gatekeepers. Britain entered the decade in recession, but that economic uncertainty also left artists free to do what they wished.

Empty buildings and industrial spaces were turned into informal venues. A 23-year-old Damien Hirst orchestrated "Freeze," a self-organized student exhibition in 1988 in a disused London warehouse. It became a landmark early art exhibition for the generation of artists known as the "Young British Artists" or YBA.

Artists Sarah Lucas and Tracey Emin opened The Shop, a temporary art gallery and social space in 1992, as a place where exhibitions could develop outside established galleries. Lucas and Emin also paved the way for women artists thanks to their deeply personal works and their edgy expressions of female liberation.

While the Spice Girls helped make feminism accessible to a younger generation of Brits in the 90s by popularizing the "girl power" slogan and shaping "identity through agency power and resistance," as argues Tate curator Helen Little, Emin and Lucas meanwhile "presented a new visual language of clothing as art to tackle societal taboos around female sexuality, vulnerability and desire" — from t-shirts with provocative slogans to a grunge look of scuffed Dr. Martens boots with razor blades. Their work "held a mirror up to gender, behavior and identity," Little writes.

blocks.caption: Sarah Lucas broke away from feminine ideals in raw works such as this 1997 photo titled 'Chicken Knickers'Image: Sarah Lucas/Sadie Coles HQ

blocks.text: Fashion and haute couture in the spotlight
At the same time, the British fashion industry came into the international spotlight.

In a feminine sensuality counter to the gender stereotypes dismissed by Emin and Lucas, waif-like Kate Moss came to represent the feminine ideal of the 1990s. Dubbed "heroin-chic," the style was an antithesis to the glamorous, athletic physiques of the supermodels who preceded her. Corinne Day's photographs of the model led to the raw aesthetic to be labelled "grunge" after the anguished style of rock music hailing from Seattle and led by Nirvana.

The trend has faced a significant cultural reexamination since: "Along with the look also came criticism that the strung-out look of drug or alcohol addiction was glamorized while encouraging serious eating disorders in a generation of young women," points out Alex Farquharson, director of the Tate Gallery in his foreword to the exhibition.

blocks.caption: The new Tate Britain exhibition includes photos of 90s icon Kate MossImage: Juergen Teller

blocks.text: The 1990s were also an exciting era for Britain in haute couture, as legendary designers John Galliano led Diorwhile Alexander McQueen started directing Givenchy at the age of 27.

McQueen's runway presentations were more akin to performance art than commercial fashion shows — and they often included historical critiques. Among them was the famous finale of his Fall/Winter 1998 collection at a London warehouse, during which the model stood in a circle of flames. Titled "Joan," the show was a reference to the killing of Joan of Arc.

McQueen designed several other runway shows that reflected on British history, with topics of conquest and punishment repeatedly coming to the forefront. His 1995 presentation "Highland Rape" referenced the history of Scotland's subjugation, with the designer describing it as "England's rape of Scotland."

blocks.caption: McQueen's fashion shows were more like performance art and included historical critiques of BritainImage: Guy Marineau/Vogue/Condé Nast

blocks.text: As co-curator Jessica Vaughan points out in her exhibition text: "Art, fashion and photography were not simply transgressive reactions … but reflected a genuine public unease with Britain's global identity and its past."

In a world that can now feel increasingly mediated by screens, algorithms and established platforms, the artwork of the 90s offers a reminder of the value of physical spaces and fresh DIY creativity of the last smartphone-free decade.

articles.title: All hail the Kult of Kemi – captain, coach and owner of the Conservatives | John Crace
articles.summary:
The Tory leader is now too big for the party to allow her to fail, so everything she does is acclaimed a work of genius

Where’s AI slop when you need it? It could all have been so much…

blocks.text: Where’s AI slop when you need it? It could all have been so much simpler. Just ask ChatGPT to write me a leader’s speech in the style of Kemi Badenoch. Make it an hour and 10 minutes long, so plenty of room for padding. Go heavy on the slogans, cliches and the obligatory crap politician jokes. Ones we’ve all heard many times before. Not least at this conference.

Make the usual digs at Labour and put the boot in to Reform. The main aim of the speech is to try to reposition a party that is tanking in third place on 20% in the polls as the main opposition to the government. And just to give everyone a reason to go home with a feeling of mild optimism, chuck in a retail offer at the end. An uncosted tax cut for people who are rich but don’t feel quite rich enough. The new multimillionaire common-or-garden lower middle classes.

Unfortunately, Kemi made the schoolgirl error of trying to write the speech for herself. And it was much the worse for it. What’s the point of having AI if you don’t use it? It was too long, too flabby. No real argument, just a collection of random thoughts. Andy Burnham in Liverpool it wasn’t. Parts of it even seemed to bore Kemi herself. As if she was going through the motions. Lazy, even. That it was still by far and away the best speech of the entire conference is not really the point. More of a reflection of how dire the others have been. Four days of the Tories in Birmingham is a trial for anyone remotely sentient.

On the surface, the Tories have seemed a happy tribe this week. There has been a soporific tranquillity to the proceedings. Few members attending, non-existent queues and above all no Robert Jenrick. Or even Liz Truss. How we miss her. But the unity feels very fragile. The Tories are now Kemi and Kemi is the Tories. The party has bet the bank on her. Kemi even now calls herself the captain, coach and owner of the Tories. Everyone else is an also-ran.

This comes at a huge risk. Because Kemi has become almost too big for the Tories to allow her to fail. So they daren’t question her. Anything she does has to be acclaimed as a work of genius. Just walking on stage is enough to secure her a standing ovation. No one has ever quite walked like that before.

blocks.caption: Delegates applaud Kemi Badenoch’s speech. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA

blocks.text: The party has been captured by the Kult of Kemi. It’s a self-fulfilling prophesy that could lead them to oblivion. They have no idea if Kemi is messiah or lemming, but they are happy to go over the cliff regardless. They are out of other options. Just don’t stop to ask why nothing the Tories seem to do is cutting through. Why the polls are stubbornly flatlining. Why it’s odds-on that beyond the few hundred people in the hall, no one will pay a blind bit of attention to her speech. It will be forgotten by tomorrow.

The morning’s proceedings began with the Tory chair, Kevin Hollinrake. Kev’s dog got a bigger cheer than Kev. Next up was the shadow justice secretary, Nick Timothy, a one-man cluster of anti-matter. No man can suck the energy out of the room like Nick. The only thing that would cheer him up is a public execution. Then the Philpster. The UK’s self-proclaimed superhero. The vigilante who took on the French. Endearingly, he still thinks the French navy knows who he is. Chris, most of the UK don’t know who you are. Nor do they care.

After this, things began to get surreal as each member of the shadow cabinet was announced and applauded as they took their seats. A bit like a third-rate talent show. The presenter still didn’t know who Nick Timothy was, despite having introduced him moments earlier. She also got Helen Whately’s name wrong. And there was one empty chair. Tom Tugendhat had invented an unmissable trip to India to get out of the embarrassment. Wise choice.

A spot of Elgar and then it was Kemi. There was a fight for the soul of the country. There’s always a fight for the soul of the country as far as the Tories are concerned. They don’t seem to realise that it was them that ripped the soul out of it. “What a great conference we’ve had,” she said. It was hard to know if she was being ironic. Other than the fact that everyone has been wandering round in brain-dead surprise that the Tories still exist, it’s been a disaster.
after newsletter promotion

After that things went weird. As if we were entering a weird dystopia. Being asked to believe the unbelievable. Like when she said that her shadow cabinet was a united team that listened to one another. This after Kemi had literally said that she was the party and that anyone who disagreed with her could go fuck themselves. The whole point of Kemi is that she listens to no one. She also had a pop at Labour for putting all their faith in one man. Pots, kettles. As for Reform, she had nothing but contempt. You’d like to think that would rule out a possible coalition.

The one moment when Kemi became truly passionate – believable even – was when she talked about race. This was Kemi at her best, talking about something she really cared about. Even if she did imagine there was no racism in football in the 70s and 80s. But this was all too short and the speech began to feel like it was dragging into eternity. We’d still be trying to stay awake well into the afternoon.

Finally the reveal. The inheritance tax cut that would be funded by as yet unspecified welfare cuts. There would be no inheritance tax on anyone leaving their home to their children. With an extra million-quid freebie thrown in, in case you needed to do it up after your parents had let it get tatty. You could hear the cheers from the country’s stately homes echo around the hall.

Here was a party that really got it. Which was prepared to do something about the cost of living for the mega rich. Even as Kemi was speaking, millions of ordinary citizens were phoning their brokers to liquidate their stock market assets so that they could upgrade their £1m homes to something far more palatial. The property market in mega-homes had just gone mental. The people’s earl, Charles Spencer, could breathe easy. Althorp was safe. Let them drink champagne.

There was just time for Kemi to pay tribute to Jeffrey Archer – the Tories have a soft spot for a convicted conman who ruined several lives – and then came the extended standing ovations. An echo chamber is going to echo.
